'''Sylvain Edward Cappell''' (born 1946) is a [[Belgian American]] mathematician specializing in [[topology]]. He is a former student of [[William Browder (mathematician)|William Browder]] at [[Princeton University]] and has spent most of his career at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]], where he is now a Silver Professor of Mathematics.

He was born in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]] and immigrated with his parents to New York City in 1950 and grew up largely in this city.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nychold.org/quest-0211.html#cappell |title=Responses to NYC DOE questionnaire |website=nychold.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040718051250/http://www.nychold.org/quest-0211.html |archive-date=2004-07-18}} </ref> In 1963, as a senior at the [[Bronx High School of Science]], he won first place in the [[Westinghouse Science Talent Search]] for his work on "The Theory of Semi-cyclical Groups with Special Reference to Non-Aristotelian Logic." He then graduated from [[Columbia University]] in 1966, winning the Van Amringe Mathematical Prize.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CCT Donors 2009–10 {{!}} Columbia College Today |url=https://www.college.columbia.edu/cct/archive/nov_dec10/donors |access-date=2022-06-04 |website=www.college.columbia.edu}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS).<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref> Cappell served as its vice president from February 2010 until January 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=2009 Election Results|publisher=American Mathematical Society|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/201002/rtx100200300p.pdf|access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=AMS Officers|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/officers/officers|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130125174547/http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/officers/officers|archive-date=2013-01-25}}</ref> He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.amacad.org/directory | title=Member Directory &#124; American Academy of Arts and Sciences }}</ref>
